page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via a KVM hypervisor, the instance supplies 16 dedicated virtual CPUs spanning 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. The memory configuration provides 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per allocation block. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

The instance relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as it includes zero local storage. For external communications, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, though no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The platform operates without dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results place the instance in mid-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7328 and a PassMark CPU score of 19093.04. However, single-core processing shows distinct constraints, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 767.49 that places it in the lower percentiles. Memory benchmarks reflect solid small-block cached throughput at 802.27 GB/s, whereas large uncached transfers drop to 30.52 GB/s read and 15.5 GB/s write throughput.

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory density, predictable multi-core throughput, and baseline 5 Gbps network interface, the ecs.g6a.4xlarge suits multi-threaded enterprise services. It is appropriate for mid-tier application servers, containerized microservices, build nodes, Redis in-memory caches, and general web serving that do not depend on high single-core clocks or direct NVMe storage access.

It adheres to an x86_64 architecture with a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions. The server includes no local disk storage, depending completely on network volumes, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps without GPU hardware. Multi-threaded benchmark testing shows balanced performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 19093.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7328, contrasted by lower single-thread execution efficiency and moderate uncached memory bandwidth. The instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as enterprise web serving, Redis caching, microservices, and general backend business logic.
